name: NGC 3389, SN 2009md field (Hubble)
blurb: NGC 3389, a spiral galaxy that hosted the faint supernova SN 2009md, seen by Hubble.
label: sn2009md-hubble
story: SN 2009md was a faint supernova, thought to come from a red supergiant near the lowest mass a star can have and still collapse and explode. Hubble returned after it faded to check that the star had disappeared.

claims.text: SN 2009md was discovered in the spiral galaxy NGC 3389
SN 2009md is a faint supernova from a low mass progenitor, a likely red supergiant near the lower mass limit for core collapse
The program images faded core-collapse supernova sites to confirm the progenitors are gone; SN 2009md is a target
